item.title: Corvus Robotics takes inventory drones into the deep freeze
item.description: Warehouses built for frozen food aren’t exactly friendly places for people, or robots. Temperatures plunge well below zero, frost builds up on everything, airflow is constant, and visibility can be a mess. Yet these same environments demand some of the most precise inventory tracking in logistics. item.title: Wisconsin Police deploy drone to catch serial park pooper
item.description: File this one under things you don’t expect drones to be used for, but here we are. A police department in Wisconsin says it used a drone, along with trail cameras, to identify and cite a woman accused of repeatedly defecating in a local public park. And yes, the drone caught the suspect in the act. more…

item.title: California city approves $683K drone program for police emergencies
item.description: The Santa Ana City Council in Orange County, California, has officially approved a new Drone as a First Responder (DFR) program, giving police a faster way to respond to emergencies while placing firm limits on how the technology can be used. more…

item.title: FPV drones show up big at 2026 Winter Olympics
item.description: The first weekend of the 2026 Milan Cortina Winter Olympics is over. Medals have already been awarded, there’s been great success and also some devastating moments. But what has been on my mind all weekend is a certain consistent buzzing noise during almost every downhill run: FPV drones. more…

item.title: New Firestorm Squall FPV drone targets modern battlefield needs
item.description: Two defense-tech companies — one focused on rapid manufacturing, the other known for battle-tested First Person View (FPV) drones — are teaming up to build what they say is a next-gen small drone designed specifically for modern combat. Firestorm Labs and Orqa have announced a partnership to produce the Firestorm Squall, a Group 1 FPV quadcopter designed to meet the needs of US and allied military forces. item.title: DJI lands game-changing drone approval in Brazil
item.description: Brazil has just handed DJI a regulatory win that could reshape how enterprise drones scale, not just in South America, but worldwide. Brazil’s National Civil Aviation Agency (ANAC) has officially granted Design Authorization for the DJI Matrice 3D series and DJI Dock 2. On paper, it’s a certification milestone. In practice, it could dramatically shorten the runway for beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) drone operations across the country. more…

item.title: Drone threat or laser test? Texas airport reopens after chaos
item.description: Air travelers in West Texas went to bed Tuesday night with no warning, and woke up to find a major American airport effectively shut down. item.title: DJI has quietly supercharged the Osmo 360
item.description: DJI recently rolled out a firmware update that fundamentally upgrades what the Osmo 360 camera can do. At the same time, the Osmo 360 Camera Adventure Combo has dropped from $700 to $511, with delivery arriving before Valentine’s Day. That’s a nearly $190 price cut on a camera that just became dramatically more creator-friendly. more…

item.title: These net-firing drone hunters will nab rogue drones over FIFA stadiums
item.description: With the 2026 FIFA World Cup set to bring more than one million international visitors to stadiums across the United States, federal security planners are moving early to counter one of the fastest-growing threats in modern event protection: small drones. more…

item.title: The DJI Mini 5 Pro drone is now even harder to ignore
